valuation_and_funding.strategic_investors_and_notes: OpenAI: $1B loan secured by warrants for 33M+ shares. Also angel investors in OpenAI leadership (Altman, Brockman, Sutskever, D’Angelo). AMD: strategic investor (Series H). Abu Dhabi Growth Fund + G42: early investors (CFIUS-cleared). OpenAI previously considered acquisition per Musk lawsuit filing.
valuation_and_funding.note_on_score_row_post_money_fields: AIBQ score rows show Post-Money $23B (matches Series H); PBQ score rows show Post-Money $4B (does not match any point on the ladder above -- reflects whatever inputs that PBQ pass used, evidently an older/unrefreshed figure). Reproduced in scores section, not folded into this ladder.

competitive_and_product.competitive_position: Primary NVIDIA challenger in AI inference. WSE-3 is 57–58x larger than leading GPU die; 900,000+ cores with 1-cycle on-chip SRAM access. Claims 15x faster inference vs. GPU at fraction of power. Took OpenAI's fast-inference business from NVIDIA (per CEO Feldman quote). CS-3 sold as 1.8-ton turnkey appliance; clusters via auxiliary devices. MemoryX for activation storage. Cloud delivery via AWS. Competition: NVIDIA (dominant CUDA ecosystem moat), Tenstorrent, Groq, SambaNova. Cerebras differentiates on latency and power; NVIDIA counters with software ecosystem depth and breadth of model support. Bull: solved a genuine inference bottleneck. Bear: CUDA moat is sticky even where WSE-3 is technically superior.
competitive_and_product.developer_ecosystem: WSE-3 available on AWS cloud platform (announced shortly after OpenAI MRA, Jan 2026). On-premise CS-3 hardware sold as turnkey system. PyTorch-compatible software stack — no proprietary framework lock-in required. Pay-as-you-go cloud access. Use case sectors: medical research, cryptography, energy, large-scale AI inference. OpenAI is the marquee enterprise reference — no meaningful open developer ecosystem as of May 2026. Inference speed advantage creates a strong reference for enterprises running large-scale LLM inference workloads.
competitive_and_product.pricing_model: Hardware sales (CS-3 AI supercomputer systems); recurring cloud-based AI services (pay-as-you-go via AWS); multi-year compute arrangements (OpenAI MRA at $10B+ deal, 750MW through 2028 with 1.25GW option to 2GW by 2030)

technology_ip.ip_activity: Core IP: wafer-scale integrated circuit architecture (WSE/WSE-2/WSE-3 generations); on-chip SRAM memory hierarchy; interconnect fabric for multi-CS-3 clusters; MemoryX storage architecture for AI model activations. Historical landmark: WSE-2 added to Computer History Museum permanent collection (Aug 2022) as 'epochal achievement in fabricating transistors.' Manufactured by TSMC (7nm process for WSE-2; WSE-3 details not fully disclosed). IP moat is architecture-level — not easily replicated on standard GPU die without fundamental wafer-scale manufacturing capability.

regulatory_governance_ownership.regulatory_exposure: Prior IPO withdrawn 2024 due to CFIUS review of G42 (UAE-based AI company) investment. Clearance received May 2025. AMD (chip competitor/partner) invested in Series H. Export controls on AI chips could affect international customers. EGC under JOBS Act (no SOX 404(b) attestation for 5 yrs).
regulatory_governance_ownership.investor_rights: Class B supervoting: 99.2% post-IPO voting power. Founders control to 5% economic stake. No meaningful public shareholder vote on board, exec comp, change-of-control, charter amendments. No SOX 404(b) up to 5 years (JOBS Act EGC).
